sop_modules.name: Metal Surface Mobilization & Access Staging
sop_modules.description: Crew mobilization, equipment staging, and scaffold/lift setup when access_type requires elevated work platforms. Scaffold and lift setup are separate line items billed per mobilization — not per LF of metal surface.

tasks.name: Crew Mobilization & Equipment Staging
tasks.description: Mobilize crew and stage equipment for exterior metal painting. Includes wire brushes, scrapers, grinders (if SP3), solvent/degreaser supplies, primer and topcoat materials, spray equipment (if spray method), and PPE (respirators for solvent work, eye protection for grinding). Metal prep generates sparks and debris — stage fire extinguisher for grinding near combustibles.

quality_notes.all: Stage all materials and equipment at work area before starting. Verify primer and topcoat compatibility. Confirm solvent/degreaser is appropriate for substrate (no oil-based products on galvanized).

tasks.name: Scaffold / Lift Setup
tasks.description: Set up scaffold or lift for elevated metal work — gutters at roofline, second-story railings, ornamental iron at height. Separate line item from painting labor. Scaffold setup includes assembly, leveling, safety rail installation, and OSHA compliance check. Lift setup includes delivery, positioning, and operator certification verification.

quality_notes.all: OSHA compliance mandatory. Scaffold on firm, level ground. Safety rails on all open sides. Lift operator must have current certification. Tag out scaffold before use.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Mobilize crew and equipment -> Scaffold/lift setup (if access_type = scaffold or lift). Complete access staging before any protection or prep work.

sop_modules.name: Metal Surface Protection & Masking
sop_modules.description: Deploy protection for landscaping, hardscape, siding, masonry junctions, light fixtures, and roof edges adjacent to metal work areas. Protection scope scales with application_method — spray method adds siding plastic sheeting upgrade. Gutter work adds roof edge protection.

tasks.name: Landscape Protection at Metal Base
tasks.description: Deploy plastic sheeting or canvas drop cloths along base of metal railings, fences, and ornamental iron to protect landscaping and plantings from prep debris (rust flakes, grinding dust) and paint drips/overspray. Metal prep generates heavy debris — use 4-6 mil plastic minimum. Secure with weights or landscape stakes.

quality_notes.all: Extend plastic 3-4 ft from metal base. Metal prep debris (rust, grinding dust) is heavier than paint chips — secure edges firmly. For spray method, extend coverage to 6-8 ft to contain drift.

tasks.name: Hardscape Protection Below Metal
tasks.description: Deploy canvas drop cloths and plastic over driveways, patios, walkways, and other hardscape surfaces below and adjacent to metal work areas. Rust converter and primer drips on concrete are extremely difficult to remove. Canvas for crew traffic areas, plastic for non-traffic.

quality_notes.all: Canvas for crew traffic (non-slip). Rust converter and primer are especially difficult to remove from concrete — prevention is critical. Extend coverage for spray method.

tasks.name: Siding Protection Behind Metal Components
tasks.description: Deploy plastic sheeting on siding behind railings, downspouts, and ornamental iron. Tape blue masking tape at metal-to-siding transition, hang plastic 4-6 ft on siding face. Upgrade to full sheeting for spray method. Prevents primer/topcoat overspray onto siding finish.

quality_notes.all: Tape at siding-to-metal transition line. Spray method requires full plastic sheeting 4-6 ft up siding. Brush method requires light tape masking only. Check for wind before spray work — overspray drift onto siding is a callback item.

tasks.name: Masonry Junction Masking
tasks.description: Tape and plastic at metal-to-masonry junctions where railings, posts, or ornamental iron meet brick, block, or stone. Polyurethane sealant at these junctions means primer/paint contact with masonry edge. Conditional — activated when metal components adjoin masonry surfaces.

quality_notes.all: Stucco tape for textured masonry. Extend masking 2-3 in. beyond junction line. Remove tape before primer/topcoat skins — pull at 45 degree angle.

tasks.name: Light Fixture Bagging & Masking
tasks.description: Bag and tape light fixtures mounted on or adjacent to metal components (porch lights on railing posts, gutter-mounted fixtures). Use plastic bags secured with masking tape. Disconnect power if accessible.

quality_notes.all: Bag fully — no exposed glass or finish. Disconnect power if accessible. Document pre-existing condition.

tasks.name: Roof Edge Protection for Gutter Work
tasks.description: Deploy drop cloth at roof shingle line where gutter attaches to fascia. Prevents primer/paint drips from staining shingles. Conditional — activated for gutter painting work only.

quality_notes.all: Lay cloth along shingle line above gutter. Weight or tape to prevent wind displacement. Primer drips on shingles = permanent stain.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Deploy all protection before any prep work begins. Landscape and hardscape first, then siding/masonry masking, then fixture bagging, then roof edge (gutter work). Metal prep generates heavy debris — protection must be in place before solvent clean.

sop_modules.name: Existing Metal Condition Assessment
sop_modules.description: Visual and tactile assessment of existing metal surface condition — rust extent, paint adhesion, structural integrity. Includes mandatory structural rust gate check. HARD STOP if structural rust (section loss, perforation) is found — structural repair is outside painting scope. Applies to existing metal substrates only (not new construction bare metal).

tasks.name: Visual & Tactile Condition Assessment
tasks.description: Assess all metal surfaces for: (1) rust extent — surface oxidation vs deep pitting, (2) existing paint adhesion — knife test, cross-hatch, fingernail lift, (3) substrate type identification — carbon steel, wrought iron, aluminum, galvanized, (4) profile complexity — standard, moderate, ornate, (5) oil/grease contamination. Document findings per component. Assessment drives prep task activation — SP1, SP2, SP3 power tool, chemical conversion, or strip-to-bare decisions flow from this assessment.

quality_notes.all: Magnet test distinguishes ferrous (steel/iron) from non-ferrous (aluminum). Check all joints, welds, and connections for rust progression. Document rust locations on sketch/photo. Assessment determines entire prep path — accuracy is critical.

tasks.name: Structural Rust / Section Loss Gate Check
tasks.description: GATE TASK — HARD STOP. Inspect all metal components for structural rust: section loss (metal thickness reduced >25%), perforation (rust-through holes), load-bearing joint failure, base plate deterioration. If structural rust is found, STOP WORK and report to project manager. Structural repair by welder/fabricator required before painting can proceed. Painting over structural rust is unsafe and outside painting scope.

gate_rules.pass_condition: No structural section loss, perforation, or load-bearing joint failure detected
gate_rules.fail_action: HARD_STOP — Report to project manager. Structural metal repair by welder/fabricator required before painting. Document with photos.

quality_notes.all: Probe all rust areas with screwdriver — surface rust flakes off, structural rust penetrates. Check base plates, post bases, weld joints, and any load-bearing connections. Section loss >25% of original thickness = structural. Document all findings with photos.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Condition assessment FIRST -> Structural rust gate check SECOND. If structural rust gate fails = HARD STOP. Assessment module must complete before prep module begins — prep task activation depends on assessment findings.

sop_modules.name: Metal Surface Preparation
sop_modules.description: Complete metal prep sequence following SSPC standards. SP 1 solvent clean is MANDATORY FIRST on ALL substrates before any mechanical prep — sanding/grinding over oily or contaminated surfaces smears contaminants into the metal profile, destroying adhesion. Subsequent prep tasks are substrate-conditional and state-conditional. Aluminum requires 15-minute prime window after cleaning — clean and prime in sections.

tasks.name: SP 1 Solvent Clean — MANDATORY FIRST
tasks.description: SSPC-SP 1 solvent cleaning — MANDATORY on ALL metal substrates BEFORE any mechanical prep. Wipe all surfaces with mineral spirits, degreaser, or appropriate solvent to remove oils, grease, dirt, and contaminants. For galvanized: use compatible degreaser (NO oil-based solvents). Sanding or grinding over contaminated surfaces smears oils into metal profile — permanent adhesion failure. Clean rags only — flip or replace when soiled.
tasks.critical_sequence_note: MUST be performed BEFORE any mechanical prep (SP2, SP3, abrading, grinding). Solvent clean first, then mechanical prep. Reversing this sequence = permanent adhesion failure.

quality_notes.all: Wipe until rags come away clean. Use clean side of rag for each pass — do not re-spread contaminants. Dispose solvent rags in fire-safe container.
quality_notes.galvanized: Use water-based degreaser or lacquer thinner — NO mineral spirits or oil-based solvents on galvanized. Oil residue prevents etch primer adhesion.
quality_notes.aluminum: Mild degreaser or lacquer thinner. Aluminum oxidizes rapidly after cleaning — prime within 15 minutes. Clean and prime in sections, NOT entire surface then prime.

tasks.name: SP 2 Hand Tool Cleaning — Wire Brush & Scraper
tasks.description: SSPC-SP 2 hand tool cleaning — wire brush and scraper to remove loose rust, loose mill scale, and loose paint. Does NOT remove tightly adhered rust or paint. Appropriate for surface rust on steel/iron where rust is not deeply pitted. Wire brush in direction of profile to reach crevices on complex profiles.

quality_notes.all: Remove all loose and flaking material. Feather edges of sound existing paint. Wire brush INTO profile crevices on ornamental iron. Do not use stainless steel wire brush on carbon steel (contamination risk is low but avoid mixing metals when possible).

tasks.name: SP 3 Power Tool Cleaning — Grinder & Wire Wheel
tasks.description: SSPC-SP 3 power tool cleaning — angle grinder with wire wheel or flap disc to remove moderate to heavy rust, tight mill scale, and tightly adhered failing paint. Provides near-white metal finish on treated areas. Reserved for QT4+ quality tiers or heavy rust conditions where SP 2 hand tool is insufficient. Generates sparks — fire extinguisher required when working near combustibles.

quality_notes.all: Grind to near-white metal on all treated areas. Feather edges to smooth transition with sound areas. Check for sparks near combustible materials — stop and relocate protection if needed. Wear full face shield for grinding overhead (gutter work).

tasks.name: Aluminum Surface Abrasion
tasks.description: Abrade aluminum surfaces with scotch-brite pad or 120-grit sandpaper to create mechanical tooth for primer adhesion. Aluminum oxide layer is smooth and non-porous — primer will not adhere without abrasion. CRITICAL: Aluminum re-oxidizes within 15 minutes of cleaning — clean and prime in sections, NOT entire surface then backtrack to prime.
tasks.critical_sequence_note: 15-MINUTE PRIME WINDOW. After abrading aluminum, primer must be applied within 15 minutes. Clean/abrade a section, prime that section, then move to next section. Do NOT abrade entire surface then return to prime — oxide layer reforms and primer adhesion fails.

quality_notes.all: Uniform matte finish after abrading — no shiny spots remaining. 120-grit maximum (finer grits do not create adequate tooth). Scotch-brite for flat areas, sandpaper for profiles. Work in 4-6 ft sections to maintain 15-minute prime window.

tasks.name: Galvanized Surface Cleaning & Passivation Removal
tasks.description: Remove passivation oils and white rust (zinc oxide) from galvanized surfaces. New galvanized has factory-applied chromate passivation that prevents paint adhesion. Weathered galvanized develops white rust (zinc oxide) that is powdery and non-adherent. Clean with white vinegar solution or proprietary galvanized cleaner. BLOCKED: Do NOT use oil-based or alkyd products on galvanized — saponification reaction destroys coating.

material_rules.block_reason: Galvanized zinc reacts with oil/alkyd binders (saponification) — coating peels within months. Acrylic DTM or etch primer ONLY.

quality_notes.all: Wipe with vinegar solution, let dwell 60 seconds, scrub with scotch-brite, rinse with clean water. Repeat until surface passes water-break test (water sheets, does not bead). Beading = residual contamination.

tasks.name: Rust Converter Application
tasks.description: Apply phosphoric acid-based rust converter to intricate/ornamental surfaces where mechanical rust removal is impractical. Converts iron oxide (rust) to iron phosphate (stable, paintable surface). Best suited for ornate profiles with crevices that wire brush and grinder cannot reach. NOT a substitute for mechanical prep on accessible flat surfaces.

quality_notes.all: Apply with brush to all rusted crevices and profiles. Allow 24-hour cure (surface turns black when converted). Do not topcoat until fully cured. Rust converter is acidic — protect adjacent surfaces from drips.

tasks.name: Degloss Existing Sound Paint
tasks.description: Abrade existing sound paint with 150-grit sandpaper or scotch-brite pad to create mechanical tooth for new primer/topcoat adhesion. Required when existing paint is sound (passes adhesion test) but surface is glossy. Do not sand through to bare metal — feather edges only at transition points.

quality_notes.all: Uniform matte finish over all glossy areas. Do not sand through to bare metal (creates adhesion boundary issues). Feather edges at sound-to-bare transitions. Wipe dust after sanding.

tasks.name: Strip Failing Paint to Sound Substrate
tasks.description: Remove all failing, peeling, cracking, and alligatored paint to sound substrate or bare metal. Combination of scraping, wire brushing, and power tool cleaning. Feather edges of sound paint at transition zones to create smooth profile. Heavy-duty prep task — production rate significantly lower than degloss.

quality_notes.all: Remove ALL loose and failing paint. Feather edges to smooth 2-3 in. transition zone. Sound paint at edges must pass knife test (no lifting when pried). Pre-1978 paint: lead test MANDATORY before any scraping or grinding.

tasks.name: Post-Mechanical-Prep Dust Cleaning
tasks.description: Remove all dust, grinding debris, rust particles, and loose material from metal surfaces after mechanical prep. Wipe with tack cloth or clean rags dampened with appropriate solvent. Critical for primer adhesion — dust particles under primer film create adhesion failure points.

quality_notes.all: Wipe until rags come away clean. Use compressed air to blow out crevices and ornamental details. Allow solvent to flash off before priming (5-10 minutes in normal conditions).

tasks.name: Polyurethane Sealant at Metal-to-Substrate Junctions
tasks.description: Apply polyurethane sealant at metal-to-wood and metal-to-masonry junctions where water infiltration can cause concealed rust. Railing post bases, gutter end caps to fascia, ornamental iron mounting plates to masonry. Polyurethane is required (not latex caulk) — metal expansion/contraction exceeds latex elasticity.

quality_notes.all: Polyurethane sealant ONLY — latex caulk fails at metal junctions due to thermal expansion mismatch. Tool joints smooth. Allow 24-hour cure before topcoating. Caulk after primer, before topcoat (primer provides adhesion surface for sealant).

sop_modules.sequence_notes: SP 1 solvent clean FIRST (mandatory, all substrates) -> SP 2 hand tool OR SP 3 power tool (steel/iron, state-dependent) -> Aluminum abrade (aluminum only) -> Galvanized clean (galvanized only) -> Rust converter (ornate + surface rust) -> Degloss (sound paint) OR Strip failing (failing paint) -> Dust clean (all, after mechanical prep) -> Caulk junctions (all). CRITICAL: SP 1 before ANY mechanical prep. Aluminum: clean/abrade/prime in sections (15-minute window).

sop_modules.name: Metal Primer Application
sop_modules.description: Apply appropriate primer based on substrate type, substrate state, and quality tier. Primer selection is the single most critical decision for metal coating longevity. Steel/iron gets DTM acrylic or alkyd primer. Galvanized/aluminum gets etch primer. Factory-finished gets bonding primer. QT5 steel gets zinc-rich primer. Epoxy primer for marginal prep situations. Spot priming for sound existing paint with bare spots.

tasks.name: DTM Acrylic Primer — Brush Application
tasks.description: Apply direct-to-metal acrylic primer by brush on steel and wrought iron surfaces. Standard primer for most exterior metal. Water-based — low VOC, fast dry, good adhesion to properly prepared ferrous metal. Brush application provides best crevice penetration on railing profiles. Work primer into all crevices, joints, and weld seams.

quality_notes.all: Work primer into all crevices and joints. No holidays (missed spots). Full wet film thickness per TDS. Check for runs on vertical surfaces. Maintain wet edge to avoid lap marks.

tasks.name: DTM Acrylic Primer — Spray Application
tasks.description: Apply direct-to-metal acrylic primer by airless spray on steel and wrought iron surfaces. Spray for long flat runs (gutters, downspouts, flat railings). MUST be followed by back-brush on complex profiles to ensure crevice coverage. Spray primer into tight areas from multiple angles.

quality_notes.all: Spray from multiple angles to reach all profiles. Back-brush all joints, crevices, and weld seams immediately after spraying (while still wet). No holidays. Full mil thickness on all surfaces including back sides of components.

tasks.name: DTM Alkyd Primer — Brush for Pitted Steel/Iron
tasks.description: Apply direct-to-metal alkyd primer by brush on pitted steel and wrought iron. Alkyd primer has superior penetration into rust pits compared to acrylic — the oil-based binder wicks into micro-pores that water-based acrylic bridges over. Reserved for surfaces with pitting from heavy rust that has been mechanically removed. BLOCKED on galvanized (saponification).

material_rules.block_reason: Alkyd binder + galvanized zinc = saponification reaction. Coating peels within months.

quality_notes.all: Work alkyd primer into pits and crevices with stiff brush. Full wet-film thickness. Allow 24-hour cure before topcoat. Alkyd primer has longer dry time than acrylic — plan schedule accordingly. Clean tools with mineral spirits.

tasks.name: Etch Primer — Galvanized & Aluminum
tasks.description: Apply etch primer (phosphoric acid self-etching) on galvanized and aluminum surfaces. Etch primer chemically bonds to non-ferrous metal surfaces where mechanical adhesion alone is insufficient. For aluminum: apply within 15 minutes of surface prep (oxide reformation window). For galvanized: apply after passivation removal and water-break test confirmation.
tasks.critical_sequence_note: Aluminum: 15-MINUTE PRIME WINDOW after cleaning/abrading. Work in sections. Galvanized: Apply only after water-break test passes (water sheets, does not bead).

quality_notes.all: Thin, even coat — etch primer is not designed for heavy build. Two thin coats better than one thick coat. Allow flash-off between coats per TDS. Do not apply in direct sun on hot metal (primer flashes too fast).

tasks.name: Bonding Primer — Factory-Finished Metal
tasks.description: Apply bonding primer on factory-finished (powder-coated, baked enamel, anodized) metal surfaces. Factory finishes are extremely smooth and non-porous — standard primers cannot achieve adequate adhesion. Bonding primer uses adhesion-promoting resins that grip smooth surfaces after light abrasion.

quality_notes.all: Light abrasion (scotch-brite) before bonding primer. Thin, even coat. Allow full cure per TDS before topcoat. Do not apply over flaking or delaminating factory finish — strip first.

tasks.name: Zinc-Rich Primer — QT5 Steel Only
tasks.description: Apply zinc-rich primer on carbon steel for QT5 premium quality tier. Zinc-rich primer provides galvanic (cathodic) corrosion protection — zinc sacrificially corrodes to protect the steel substrate. Premium system for maximum corrosion resistance. Requires thoroughly cleaned bare metal substrate (SP 3 minimum).

quality_notes.all: Stir thoroughly — zinc particles settle rapidly. Maintain wet film thickness per TDS (zinc content must meet minimum for cathodic protection). Apply to near-white metal only (SP 3 prep minimum). Allow 24-hour cure before topcoat.

tasks.name: Epoxy Primer — Marginal Prep Situations
tasks.description: Apply two-component epoxy primer for marginal prep situations where surface preparation is less than ideal (e.g., rust in inaccessible crevices, incomplete mill scale removal). Epoxy provides superior adhesion and moisture barrier on imperfectly prepared surfaces. CRITICAL: 24-72 hour recoat window — topcoat MUST be applied before window expires or adhesion to epoxy surface fails. Mix ratio is critical — follow TDS exactly.

recoat_window.consequence_of_exceeding: Epoxy surface becomes too hard and smooth for topcoat adhesion. Must abrade (sand) cured epoxy before topcoating if window is exceeded.

quality_notes.all: Mix ratio is CRITICAL — follow TDS exactly. Pot life is limited (4-8 hours typical). Apply within pot life. MUST topcoat within 24-72 hour recoat window. Schedule topcoat day before mixing epoxy primer. Exceeding recoat window requires sanding before topcoat.

tasks.name: Spot Prime Bare Areas on Existing Metal
tasks.description: Spot prime bare metal areas where existing sound paint has been removed or worn through. Apply appropriate primer (based on substrate type) to bare spots only — feather edges to overlap 1-2 in. onto sound existing paint. For sound existing paint that has been deglossed, spot priming is more efficient than full prime coat.

quality_notes.all: Prime all bare metal spots. Feather primer edges 1-2 in. onto sound adjacent paint. No holidays on bare metal. Allow full cure before topcoat. Match primer type to substrate type (DTM acrylic for steel/iron, etch for galvanized/aluminum).

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Primer selection follows substrate_type and substrate_state: Steel/iron → DTM acrylic (standard) or DTM alkyd (pitted) or zinc-rich (QT5). Galvanized/aluminum → etch primer. Factory-finished → bonding primer. Epoxy → marginal prep. Spot prime → existing metal with bare spots. CRITICAL: Aluminum 15-minute window. Epoxy 24-72 hour recoat window. Galvanized + alkyd = BLOCKED.

sop_modules.name: Metal Finish Coat Application
sop_modules.description: Apply DTM acrylic finish coat by brush, spray, or spray_backbrush method. Brush is primary method for complex profiles (railings, ornamental iron). Spray for flat runs (gutters, downspouts). Spray on metal with any profile complexity = mandatory back-brush for crevice coverage. Ornamental detail brush for intricate elements. Two-coat system standard — first coat in this module, second coat after interstage.

tasks.name: DTM Acrylic Finish — Brush Application
tasks.description: Apply DTM acrylic finish coat by brush. Primary method for railings, ornamental iron, and any metal with profile complexity. Brush provides best crevice penetration and film build control on vertical/complex surfaces. Work paint into all joints, welds, and crevices. Maintain wet edge — metal dries fast in sun/wind.

quality_notes.QT3: Full coverage, no holidays. Uniform finish. Work paint into all crevices.
quality_notes.QT4: Full coverage, no holidays. Smooth, even finish with minimal brush marks. Inspect for thin spots on edges and high points.
quality_notes.QT5: Premium finish. No brush marks visible at arm's length. Full crevice coverage. Inspect under raking light for thin spots. Touch up immediately.

tasks.name: DTM Acrylic Finish — Spray Application
tasks.description: Apply DTM acrylic finish coat by airless spray on flat metal runs — gutters, downspouts, flat railing sections. Spray provides fastest production rate on long straight runs. NOT sufficient alone for any surface with joints, crevices, or profiles — must be followed by back-brush task for crevice coverage.

quality_notes.all: Maintain consistent distance and speed. Overlap passes 50%. Multiple angles on profiles. Full mil thickness on all surfaces. Check for holidays on back sides and undersides.

tasks.name: DTM Acrylic Finish — Spray + Back-Brush
tasks.description: Spray DTM acrylic finish coat followed by immediate back-brushing for crevice coverage on profiled metal surfaces. Spray deposits material, back-brush works it into joints, welds, crevices, and ornamental details. Mandatory method when spraying any metal with profile complexity. One person sprays, second person follows with brush while coating is still wet.

quality_notes.all: Back-brush IMMEDIATELY after spray pass — while coating is still wet. Do not allow spray coat to skin before back-brushing (lap marks). Work brush into all crevices, joints, and ornamental details. Two-person operation: sprayer + brusher working in tandem.

tasks.name: Ornamental Detail Brush Work
tasks.description: Detail brush application for intricate ornamental iron elements — scrollwork, rosettes, finials, basket weave, twisted bar details. These elements cannot be adequately coated by standard brush or spray alone. Small artist-type brushes for tight crevices. Activated when profile_complexity = ornate and item = ITM_METAL_ORNAMENTAL.

quality_notes.all: Detail brush ALL ornamental crevices. Check for holidays in scrollwork and tight curves. Multiple light coats better than one heavy coat on intricate details (prevents drips). Inspect with flashlight for missed spots in deep crevices.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Apply finish coat by method: brush (complex profiles), spray (flat runs), or spray_backbrush (profiled surfaces). Ornamental detail brush is supplemental task for ornate elements. Spray on metal = always back-brush crevices. No roll method — excluded for metal profiles.

sop_modules.name: Metal Final Inspection & Touch-Up
sop_modules.description: Final inspection of all coated metal surfaces for holidays, thin spots, drips, runs, and crevice coverage deficiencies. Touch up all defects before declaring coat complete. Inspection drives interstage — coat 1 must pass inspection before coat 2 proceeds.

tasks.name: Final Coat Inspection
tasks.description: Inspect all coated metal surfaces for: (1) holidays — missed spots, especially in crevices and back sides, (2) thin spots — edges, high points, and weld seams where coating pulls away, (3) drips and runs — vertical surfaces and undersides, (4) crevice coverage — joints, welds, ornamental details. Use flashlight in crevices. Mark defects for touch-up.

quality_notes.QT3: Check for holidays and major defects. All surfaces must have full coverage.
quality_notes.QT4: Detailed inspection. Check crevices with flashlight. Mark all thin spots and holidays. No visible drips or runs.
quality_notes.QT5: Premium inspection. Raking light check. Mil thickness verification on accessible surfaces. All crevices fully coated. No defects visible at arm's length.

tasks.name: Touch Up Holidays & Defects
tasks.description: Touch up all marked defects from inspection: brush-coat holidays, feather thin spots, cut drips and re-coat runs, detail-brush missed crevices. Touch-up must match surrounding finish — no visible demarcation. Touch up while same batch of paint is available (color match).

quality_notes.all: Brush-coat holidays. Sand drips smooth (220-grit) and re-coat. Feather touch-up edges to blend with surrounding finish. Use same paint batch for color match. Re-inspect after touch-up.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Inspect ALL surfaces after each coat -> Touch up defects -> Re-inspect touch-up areas. Inspection quality scales with quality_tier.

sop_modules.name: Metal Project Cleanup & Demobilization
sop_modules.description: Remove all protection, tear down scaffold/lift if applicable, clean tools, dispose waste materials properly (solvents, rust converter, grinding dust), and demobilize from site. Solvent waste disposal must follow local environmental regulations.

tasks.name: Remove All Protection & Masking
tasks.description: Remove all drop cloths, plastic sheeting, masking tape, and fixture bags. Inspect for paint drips or debris on protected surfaces — clean up any contamination before releasing protection. Remove tape at 45-degree angle to prevent surface damage.

quality_notes.all: Remove all masking tape before adhesive bakes on (sun exposure hardens adhesive). Inspect protected surfaces for drips — clean immediately. Fold drop cloths paint-side-in.

tasks.name: Scaffold / Lift Teardown
tasks.description: Disassemble scaffold or arrange lift pickup. Inspect scaffold components for paint contamination — clean before return if rented. Conditional — activated when scaffold or lift was used (mirrors setup task).

quality_notes.all: Disassemble in reverse of setup. Inspect for paint overspray on scaffold components — clean before return if rented. Stage for pickup.

tasks.name: Tool Cleaning, Waste Disposal & Demobilization
tasks.description: Clean all tools and equipment. Dispose of solvent rags in fire-safe container (spontaneous combustion risk). Dispose of rust converter, epoxy waste, and grinding dust per local environmental regulations. Bag and dispose of all debris. Final site walkthrough — leave work area cleaner than found.

quality_notes.all: Solvent rags in fire-safe container — NEVER ball up in trash bag (spontaneous combustion). Rust converter and epoxy waste may be hazardous — follow local disposal regulations. Final walkthrough to confirm no debris, drips, or damage.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Remove protection -> Scaffold teardown (if applicable) -> Tool cleaning -> Waste disposal -> Final walkthrough -> Demobilize.

round_configurations.name: New Construction Bare Metal — Primer + 2 Finish Coats
round_configurations.description: Full system for bare metal (new construction or stripped to bare). Full primer coat followed by two finish coats with interstage inspection. Standard for SS_EXT_BARE_METAL on steel, wrought iron, and galvanized.
round_configurations.notes: Full primer + 2 finish coats. Primer type selected by substrate_type (DTM acrylic/alkyd for steel/iron, etch for galvanized/aluminum, zinc-rich for QT5 steel). Interstage inspection between coat 1 and coat 2.

round_configurations.name: Factory-Primed Metal — Bonding Primer + 2 Finish Coats
round_configurations.description: System for factory-primed or powder-coated metal. Bonding primer over factory finish, then two finish coats. Factory finish provides base protection but is not designed for field topcoat adhesion — bonding primer bridges the gap.
round_configurations.notes: Bonding primer over factory finish + 2 finish coats. Light abrasion before bonding primer. Factory finish must be sound — strip any delaminating areas before priming.

round_configurations.name: Existing Sound Paint — Spot Prime + 2 Finish Coats
round_configurations.description: System for existing metal with sound paint. Degloss existing surface, spot prime any bare areas, then two finish coats. Most efficient path for existing metal in good condition.
round_configurations.notes: Degloss + spot prime bare areas + 2 finish coats. Assessment module activates first (existing only). No full primer coat needed — spot prime bare areas only.

round_configurations.name: Existing Surface Rust — Full Prep + Primer + 2 Finish Coats
round_configurations.description: System for existing metal with surface rust. Full mechanical prep (SP2/SP3), rust converter on ornate profiles, full primer coat, then two finish coats. Assessment module includes structural rust gate check.
round_configurations.notes: Assessment (incl. structural rust gate) + full mechanical prep + full primer + 2 finish coats. Rust converter added for ornate profiles. SP3 power tool at QT4+. Structural rust = HARD STOP.

round_configurations.name: Existing Failing Paint — Strip + Full Prep + Primer + 2 Finish Coats
round_configurations.description: Most intensive round configuration. Strip all failing paint, mechanical prep to sound substrate or bare metal, full primer coat, two finish coats. Assessment module includes structural rust gate. Pre-1978 paint requires lead testing before any scraping.
round_configurations.notes: Assessment (incl. structural rust gate) + strip failing paint + full mechanical prep + full primer + 2 finish coats. Most labor-intensive configuration. Lead test mandatory for pre-1978 structures.

key_metal_rules_enforced: SP 1 solvent clean MANDATORY FIRST before any mechanical prep — sanding over oils smears contaminants into metal profile.
Structural rust = HARD STOP gate task — section loss, perforation, or joint failure is outside painting scope. Report to PM.
Aluminum 15-minute prime window — clean/abrade and prime in sections. Do NOT clean entire surface then return to prime.
Galvanized + oil-based/alkyd = BLOCKED — saponification reaction destroys coating within months.
Brush is primary method for complex metal profiles. Spray on metal = mandatory back-brush for crevice coverage.
Epoxy primer 24-72 hour recoat window — must topcoat before window expires or sand cured epoxy for adhesion.
No roll method — excluded for metal profiles. Brush, spray, or spray_backbrush only.
Polyurethane sealant (not latex caulk) at metal-to-substrate junctions — thermal expansion mismatch exceeds latex elasticity.

assumptions.value: SSPC-SP 1 solvent clean is MANDATORY before any mechanical prep on all metal substrates without exception.
assumptions.source: Exterior_Metal_Surfaces_Doctrine.md: SP 1 removes oils and contaminants that mechanical prep would smear into the metal profile. SSPC standard sequence: SP 1 → SP 2/SP 3.
assumptions.note: Industry standard per SSPC. Violation = permanent adhesion failure.

assumptions.value: Structural rust (section loss >25%, perforation, load-bearing joint failure) is a HARD STOP — painting over structural rust is unsafe and outside painting scope.
assumptions.source: Exterior_Metal_Surfaces_Doctrine.md: Structural integrity assessment required before any metal painting. Structural repair by welder/fabricator is prerequisite.
assumptions.note: Safety and liability issue. Not a paintable condition.

assumptions.value: Aluminum must be primed within 15 minutes of cleaning/abrading. Work in sections — do not clean entire surface then return to prime.
assumptions.source: Exterior_Metal_Surfaces_Doctrine.md: Aluminum oxide layer reforms rapidly after cleaning. Etch primer must contact fresh aluminum surface for chemical bond.
assumptions.note: Well-documented metallurgical property. Section-by-section workflow is standard professional practice.

assumptions.value: Oil-based and alkyd products are BLOCKED on galvanized metal. Zinc reacts with alkyd binder (saponification) causing coating failure within months.
assumptions.source: Exterior_Metal_Surfaces_Doctrine.md: Saponification is a chemical reaction between zinc and oil/alkyd binders. Acrylic DTM or etch primer only on galvanized.

assumptions.value: Two finish coats are standard for all exterior metal painting. Metal thermal cycling (expansion/contraction) stresses single-coat films beyond their elastic limit.
assumptions.source: Exterior_Metal_Surfaces_Doctrine.md: Metal substrates experience greater thermal cycling than wood — coating film must have sufficient build and elasticity to resist cracking.
assumptions.note: Two coats minimum for all round configurations regardless of substrate state.

assumptions.value: Roll application method is excluded for metal surfaces. Metal profiles (railings, gutters, ornamental) are not conducive to roller application.
assumptions.source: Exterior_Metal_Surfaces_Doctrine.md: Metal profiles are too narrow and complex for roller application. Brush, spray, and spray_backbrush are the permitted methods.
assumptions.note: Physical constraint of metal geometry. Brush is primary, spray is supplemental.

assumptions.value: Epoxy primer has a 24-72 hour recoat window. Topcoat must be applied within this window or cured epoxy surface must be abraded for adhesion.
assumptions.source: Exterior_Metal_Surfaces_Doctrine.md: Epoxy cures to a hard, smooth surface that subsequent coats cannot adhere to without mechanical tooth. Recoat within window while surface is still chemically receptive.
assumptions.note: Schedule topcoat day before mixing epoxy. Exceeding window adds sanding step.

assumptions.value: Polyurethane sealant (not latex caulk) is required at metal-to-substrate junctions. Metal thermal expansion/contraction exceeds latex caulk elasticity.
assumptions.source: Exterior_Metal_Surfaces_Doctrine.md: Metal coefficient of thermal expansion is ~2x wood. Latex caulk fails at metal joints — polyurethane maintains elasticity across thermal cycling range.
assumptions.note: Polyurethane sealant is more expensive but mandatory for metal junction durability.

exclusions.reason: Metal profiles (railings, gutters, downspouts, ornamental iron) are not conducive to roller application. Brush, spray, and spray_backbrush are the only permitted methods.
Structural rust repair is outside painting scope. Gate task TSK_METL_STRUCTURAL_RUST_CHECK enforces HARD STOP when structural section loss is found. Welder/fabricator required.

Abrasive blasting is industrial/commercial prep (SSPC-SP 6, SP 10). Residential exterior metal spec covers hand tool (SP 2) and power tool (SP 3) cleaning only. Blasting requires containment and specialized equipment beyond residential scope.
Factory process — not field-applicable. Zinc-rich primer (QT5) is the field equivalent for maximum corrosion protection on carbon steel.
This spec covers exterior metal only. Interior metal (stair railings, decorative iron) is a separate spec family with different environmental exposure and prep requirements.

exclusions.excluded_item: Oil-based / alkyd topcoat on any substrate
exclusions.reason: DTM acrylic is the standard topcoat system for all exterior metal. Alkyd primer is permitted for pitted steel/iron (superior pit penetration) but alkyd topcoat is not specified — acrylic DTM topcoat over alkyd primer is the correct system.
